$Comment: The Voidtaken Horseman, the restless graveyard's boss wave every fifth wave of its endless run: the Headless Horseman in the saddle as the void took him, his own look (Appearance, the model Hallows_Eve_Headless_Horseman_Mounted, the horse walking and galloping as he flies) wrapped in the void's glow. He is a Variant of the Horseman's normal ride, Hallows_Eve_Headless_Horseman_Mounted, so he flies and fights as that file says, and Modify names only the Parameters it declares for what the void changes. He flies the Horseman's ride with the void in it (Seasons_Of_Orbis_Voidtaken_Ride, CombatAdditionalBehaviorComponent, which runs Hallows_Eve_Horseman_Ride with void bombs on its bomb pass): dives to fight low, wide high swings, laps of the fountain, swoops through a ringed spot and bomb passes. Between moves he hurls a void bomb (Root_Seasons_Of_Orbis_Voidtaken_Bomb) at a player within 18 blocks, but only after aiming at them for 2 seconds (RangedAttackAimingRange, the game's own flier aim tell), then waits 3 to 4 seconds (RangedAttackPauseRange); it bursts in the void and leaves the ground burning, hurting players only. MaxHealth is his own, written here so a change to the Horseman's fight never moves him: he has no party health steps, and each return the run's ramp makes him tougher (the dungeon's Run.Endless.Ramp, per return). Nothing calls him back toward the plaza (the run sends no Orbis_Boss_Leash), so he follows his target anywhere in the graveyard. His own _CombatConfig replaces the Horseman's whole: Seasons_Of_Orbis_Voidtaken_Ward, under which the void hurts him at half and which gives him his glow. He dies in the void (DeathParticles Effect_Death_Void) and drops nothing (the Horseman's DropList Empty): his reward is what each boss wave banks into the run's chest. A key the Horseman's role does not declare under Parameters makes the game refuse the whole role.
